title: Leo’s Criticisms of Trump Are Very American
author: Julia Yost
content:
![Leo’s Criticisms of Trump Are Very
American](https://storage.ghost.io/c/65/af/65afbdb5-30bf-4286-acc4-9535069adb42/content/images/2026/04/GettyImages-2238565185-1-1.jpg)

Last spring, for the first time in history, an American was elected pope. Many
hoped that Leo XIV would act as a counterweight to Donald Trump. Others hoped
that he would be content to shepherd the world's 1.4 billion Catholics and let
someone else be the face of the global resistance.

Leo reigned quietly until Trump started a war with Iran. Leo
[_lamented_](https://x.com/Pontifex/status/2028086271021613489?ref=compactmag.com)
the war, as any modern pope would. Since then, tensions between the White
House and the Vatican have escalated in an unprecedented way. The essential
blame lies with Trump, for his gross intemperance. And at the height of the
controversy, Leo is still far from being the resistance pope. But the
dismaying spectacle reveals a downside for American Catholics in having a pope
who takes American affairs so much to heart.
